items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: here's another thing of my Sextet, with Marshall Royal, Maxwell Davis, Floyd Turner, Eddie Beal, and with Chico Hamilton on drums

ctx.x: I'm looking over some other things. There was the Red Callender Trio with Willie McDaniel, Lucky Enois, and I had a thing on there, "Red Light." That was on the Black-and-White label. "By the River St. Marie" and "Red Boogie". "Red Light" was a minor hit around town. Remember that? One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, Red Light, and then we'd go into the Blues, and Leonard Enois would sing some Blues choruses. That was kind of fun. That was a fun period.

And here's another thing of my Sextet, with Marshall Royal, Maxwell Davis, Floyd Turner, Eddie Beal, and with Chico Hamilton on drums and Albert Calderone on timbales. This is one where I remember doing "Perdido" bossa-nova style, which was probably way ahead of its time. They didn't release that one. And there were another two things, "Fooled Again" and "Don't Lend Me No Money," unissued on RCA-Victor. "Midnight With Sampson." There was a guy called Bill Sampson who had a disk jockey show that came on at…

items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Red and I worked quite a bit together. As a matter of fact, Red Callender, and myself, and Dudley Brooks, piano player, we were on staff at Paramount Studios.

ctx.x: Anyway, I started taking lessons from Lee because Lee was playing with Lorenzo Flennoy at the time, the band, with Red Callender, Lee, Red Mack, you know, those guys. Anyway I’m in high school and all of a sudden Lee had me to sub for him every now and then.
Because you had been studying with him, he knew you could handle it.
